data.long_meaning: The name Alakesh is derived from the Sanskrit language, meaning 'ruler of the universe'. In Hindu mythology, Alakesh is an epithet of various gods, particularly Lord Vishnu and Shiva, representing their supreme power and dominion over the cosmos. The name Alakesh carries the meaning “Ruler of the universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Alakesh usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The name Alakesh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Alakh' meaning 'invisible' or 'beyond perception'. One historical reference is Alakh Alakhshah, a legendary king in Hindu mythology who was said to rule over the invisible realm of the universe. He is believed to have appeared during the Mahabharata period, which dates from around 400 BCE to 300 CE.

Another reference to the name Alakesh is Alakh Nand, a ruler of the Karnata Chalukya Empire in India during the 12th century CE. He is known for his military conquests and patronage of art and culture.
